Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
Now about things offered to images: we all seem to ourselves to have knowledge. Knowledge gives pride, but love gives true strength.
論到祭偶像之物，我們曉得我們都有知識。但知識是叫人自高自大，惟有愛心能造就人。
The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.
If anyone seems to himself to have knowledge, so far he has not the right sort of knowledge about anything;
若有人以為自己知道甚麼，按他所當知道的，他仍是不知道。
But the one who loves God is known by God.
But if anyone has love for God, God has knowledge of him.
若有人愛神，這人乃是神所知道的。
So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.
So, then, as to the question of taking food offered to images, we are certain that an image is nothing in the world, and that there is no God but one.
論到吃祭偶像之物，我們知道偶像在世上算不得甚麼，也知道神只有一位，再沒有別的神。
For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as there are many so-called gods and lords),
For though there are those who have the name of gods, in heaven or on earth, as there are a number of gods and a number of lords,
雖有稱為神的，或在天，或在地，就如那許多的神，許多的主；
yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.
There is for us only one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we are for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we have our being through him.
然而我們只有一位神，就是父─萬物都本於他；我們也歸於他─並有一位主，就是耶穌基督─萬物都是藉著他有的；我們也是藉著他有的。
But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.

Still, all men have not that knowledge: but some, being used till now to the image, are conscious that they are taking food which has been offered to the image; and because they are not strong in the faith, their minds are troubled.
但人不都有這等知識。有人到如今因拜慣了偶像，就以為所吃的是祭偶像之物。他們的良心既然軟弱，也就污穢了。
But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.
But God's approval of us is not based on the food we take: if we do not take it we are no worse for it; and if we take it we are no better.
其實食物不能叫神看中我們，因為我們不吃也無損，吃也無益。
Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
But take care that this power of yours does not give cause for trouble to the feeble.
只是你們要謹慎，恐怕你們這自由竟成了那軟弱人的絆腳石。
For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?
For if a man sees you, who have knowledge, taking food as a guest in the house of an image, will it not give him, if he is feeble, the idea that he may take food offered to images?
若有人見你這有知識的，在偶像的廟裡坐席，這人的良心若是軟弱，豈不放膽去吃那祭偶像之物嗎？
So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
And so, through your knowledge, you are the cause of destruction to your brother, for whom Christ underwent death.
因此，基督為他死的那軟弱弟兄，也就因你的知識沉淪了。
By sinning against your brothers in this way and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
And in this way, doing evil to the brothers, and causing trouble to those whose faith is feeble, you are sinning against Christ.
你們這樣得罪弟兄們，傷了他們軟弱的良心，就是得罪基督。
Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.
For this reason, if food is a cause of trouble to my brother, I will give up taking meat for ever, so that I may not be a cause of trouble to my brother.
所以，食物若叫我弟兄跌倒，我就永遠不吃肉，免得叫我弟兄跌倒了。
